overview: This file traces the development of dismissal and retirement allowances in Japan from customary labor practice toward statutory regulation between 1933 and 1936. It combines consular reporting, a newspaper survey, State Department correspondence arising from the case of a long-serving Japanese commercial employee, and findings on how major Japanese firms calculated allowances according to final salary and years of service. The file culminates in an embassy despatch and full English translation of Japan’s 1936 Law No. 42, which required qualifying factories and mines to establish retirement reserves and provide allowances.
interest: Shows informal corporate retirement customs preceding statutory regimes, via one employee's case and the translated 1936 retirement-reserve law.
